data.decision: The optimistic live-filter 4x2 MAC-step saving is far below the 3% two-model expansion trigger, while a dual weight/parameter path would add implementation and timing risk. Defer RTL/route/board for this mapping; padded planes and 16-MAC architecture are separate experiments.

kws.boundary: No credit for cache, layout, control, parameter, output, or clock effects.

vww.boundary: No credit for cache, layout, control, parameter, output, or clock effects.

data.qualification: The step calculation is a bound on lane-utilization benefit, not on all possible redesign side effects. It optimistically pairs arbitrary live channels; the adjacent-only case is reported separately. Weight-byte selection events are internal datapath demands, not SDRAM transactions. Output quantization and byte writes remain serialized.
data.scope: Boardless arithmetic-step gate for frozen KWS/VWW with exact constant filters skipped; no 4x2 RTL or physical speedup claim.

sixteen_mac_separate_gate.conclusion: Raw DSP count does not rule out 16 MACs, but this route has only 2 free BSRAM, 406 free CLS and 0.028 MHz clock margin. A second weight stream, delivery/control, accumulation, and routed timing need a separate exact RTL prototype. A 4x2 mapping still uses only eight products per cycle and is not a 16-MAC experiment.

data.proof_scope: The unchanged raw descriptor checks bound legal dimensions before execution; narrowed products retain all bits reachable from legal descriptors. No FSM state or output arithmetic changed. Each other generated engine snapshot still needs its own RTL regression and Gowin route.
